title: Duplicate metoprolol MAR entry for MRN-334521
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240603-0128
MRN: MRN-334521
Encounter: ENC-ADM-33452
Reported: 2024-06-03 07:45
Severity: P0 — patient safety

Issue: Care coordinator reported two identical metoprolol 25 mg orders at 08:00 in the MAR for MRN-334521. Patient had not received either dose. Pharmacy verified the order appeared twice due to a concurrent write conflict (BUG-EHR-2301).

Immediate action: Pharmacy lead notified within 15 minutes. Duplicate order deleted. MAR-DISCREPANCY flag applied. Safety event filed in RL Solutions under code MED-DISP-ERR. Correct dose administered at 09:15 after pharmacist confirmation.

Root cause: BUG-EHR-2301 — concurrent medication order de-duplication failure in the EHR ordering module. Two sessions submitted the same order within a 200 ms window; the de-dup lock was not acquired correctly.

Runbook referenced: ICD-MED-004
Status: Resolved. Bug still active (fix pending next maintenance window).

title: Lab result HL7 routing failure for MRN-293847
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240512-0209
MRN: MRN-293847
Lab Order: LAB-293847-0209
Reported: 2024-05-12 14:30
Severity: P1

Issue: CBC with differential ordered for MRN-293847 (ward: General Medicine 2A) did not appear in the EHR chart 4 hours after the lab completed processing. Lab confirmed result was transmitted; HL7 listener showed ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL in the routing log.

Immediate action: Coordinator escalated to hl7-support@healthcare-app.internal. HL7 support team manually re-routed the message within 90 minutes. Result appeared in chart at 17:45.

Root cause: ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL — intermittent HL7 v2.x routing failure affecting lab result delivery. The HL7 listener dropped messages with MSH-11 value 'D' (debug mode) instead of 'P' (production).

Status: Resolved for this ticket. ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL remains under active monitoring.

title: LTC medication sync failure on admission for MRN-847392
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240415-0077
MRN: MRN-847392
Encounter: ENC-ADM-84739
Reported: 2024-04-15 10:20
Severity: P1

Issue: LTC patient MRN-847392 was admitted from a partner facility. The LTC medication sync timed out silently. Coordinator did not notice the failure and proceeded to the medication reconciliation step with an incomplete medication list. Pharmacist caught the discrepancy during countersign review.

Immediate action: Pharmacist placed a hold on all new medication orders. Coordinator manually entered prior medications from the referring facility's fax. LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag applied. Pharmacist countersigned after complete list was entered.

Root cause: BUG-EHR-2201 — LTC sync module failure on admission transfer.

Lesson: When admitting LTC patients (patient_tier: plus), always verify the medication list is complete before proceeding. If LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag must be applied, notify pharmacist immediately rather than proceeding independently.

title: Post-discharge patient unable to book follow-up — SCH-CONFLICT-88
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240520-0301
MRN: MRN-556123
Encounter: ENC-DIS-55612
Reported: 2024-05-20 16:45
Severity: P1

Issue: Patient MRN-556123 was discharged on 2024-05-19. They called the next day unable to book a follow-up with their cardiologist, receiving error SCH-CONFLICT-88.

Immediate action: Coordinator manually booked the follow-up via the phone scheduling line. Patient was satisfied.

Root cause: BUG-SCH-0445 — discharge record not yet propagated to the scheduling availability index. Patient tried to book within 24 hours of discharge.

Prevention noted: Per ICD-DIS-003, follow-up appointments should be booked before discharge. This was not done for MRN-556123. Care team reminded of best practice.

title: AUTH-4012 blocking admission pre-authorization for MRN-412033
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240601-0411
MRN: MRN-412033
Encounter: ENC-ADM-41203
Reported: 2024-06-01 09:15
Severity: P1

Issue: Pre-authorization submission for elective MRI for MRN-412033 failed with error AUTH-4012. Admission was on hold pending authorization.

Immediate action: Coordinator identified AUTH-4012 as an expired token error per ICD-INS-001. Refreshed the auth credentials in the Insurance Verification module and re-submitted. Authorization approved within 40 minutes.

Root cause: The payer rotated their API keys overnight and the cached token was expired. AUTH-4012 is not a denial — it is an authentication failure. Re-submission with fresh credentials resolved the issue.

Lesson: When seeing AUTH-4012, do not interpret as a denial. Always re-submit with refreshed credentials before escalating.

title: Telehealth session TC-CONN-FAIL for MRN-678234
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240528-0188
MRN: MRN-678234
Reported: 2024-05-28 11:00
Severity: P2

Issue: Patient MRN-678234 attempted to join a scheduled telehealth session via the HealthConnect mobile app (iOS). Received TC-CONN-FAIL immediately on joining.

Immediate action: Coordinator guided patient through app.healthcare-app.com/device-check. Device check identified: HealthConnect app version 4.1 (below minimum 4.2). Patient updated the app. Session joined successfully on second attempt.

Root cause: Outdated HealthConnect mobile app. Version 4.1 uses deprecated WebRTC library that fails on iOS 17.4+ due to security policy changes.

Lesson: Direct patients to device-check first — it quickly identifies version issues. Note app version 4.2+ requirement per ICD-TC-001.

title: Critical lab result not delivered to EHR for MRN-901234
content:
Ticket ID: PT-20240610-0502
MRN: MRN-901234
Lab Order: LAB-901234-0610
Reported: 2024-06-10 08:30
Severity: P0 — critical lab value delayed

Issue: Potassium critical high result (OBX-8=HH, K=6.8 mEq/L) for MRN-901234 was completed by the lab at 07:45 but did not appear in the EHR chart. Ordering physician did not receive critical value page. Nurse noticed the delay during morning rounds and escalated.

Immediate action: Coordinator called hl7-support@healthcare-app.internal immediately. HL7 support team manually re-routed the ORU^R01 message. Result appeared in chart at 09:05. Physician notified directly by phone. Patient received emergency potassium management.

Root cause: ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL — the critical value message was dropped because MSH-11 was set to 'D' on the lab's interface. The automated critical-value page also failed because it depends on chart delivery.

Lesson: Always call hl7-support directly for critical lab values — do not wait for the standard 90-minute resolution window.

title: Duplicate lisinopril order in MAR for MRN-223344
content:

Root cause: BUG-EHR-2301 — concurrent order submission during attending's morning rounds when multiple staff were entering orders simultaneously.

title: MRN not found on admission — new patient referred from external facility
content:

Lesson: For external referrals, always check with HIM before concluding the patient is unregistered. MPI merge issues can cause records to appear missing even when they exist.

title: HealthConnect portal activation email not received by new patient

title: Plus patient LTC transfer — incomplete medication list missed at admission

Lesson: For all patient_tier=plus admissions from LTC facilities, explicitly verify the medication count against the referral document before proceeding.

title: Scheduling conflict SCH-CONFLICT-55 — patient flagged as admitted post-discharge

title: Lab order LAB-551122-0516 delayed — ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL

title: AUTH-4012 misread as denial — elective surgery delayed for MRN-334567

Issue: Pre-authorization for elective knee arthroscopy for MRN-334567 failed with AUTH-4012. Surgery was scheduled for the following morning. Coordinator initially escalated as a denial, causing unnecessary delay.

Immediate action: Supervisor identified AUTH-4012 as an expired token (not a denial) per ICD-INS-001. Coordinator refreshed token and re-submitted. Authorization approved within 1 hour. Surgery proceeded on schedule.

Root cause: Coordinator misinterpreted AUTH-4012 as a payer denial. Training gap identified.

Action taken: All coordinators reminded that AUTH-4012 = expired token. Escalation checklist updated to distinguish AUTH-4012 from actual denials.

title: Concurrent medication order de-duplication failure
content:
Bug ID: BUG-EHR-2301
Component: EHR Ordering Module — MAR write path
Discovered: 2024-05-28
Severity: P0 — patient safety risk

Description: When two browser sessions submit an identical medication order for the same patient within approximately 200 ms, the de-duplication lock is not acquired correctly. Both orders are written to the MAR, resulting in a duplicate. This has been observed primarily with metoprolol and lisinopril orders during shift handover.

Impact: Duplicate medication entries in MAR. Risk of double-dosing if not caught by pharmacy review.

Workaround: Pharmacy must complete MAR review within 30 minutes of any new medication order. Coordinators should apply MAR-DISCREPANCY flag when a duplicate is suspected and notify pharmacy lead immediately.

ETA: Next scheduled maintenance window.
Assignee: EHR Platform Team
Related tickets: PT-20240603-0128, PT-20240507-0099

title: Long-term care medication sync failure on admission transfer
content:
Bug ID: BUG-EHR-2201
Component: LTC Medication Sync — Admission Transfer Module
Discovered: 2024-04-10
Severity: P1

Description: When a long-term care (LTC) patient is transferred from a partner facility and admitted via the web portal, the medication reconciliation module fails to pull the prior facility's medication list from the state LTC registry. The sync call times out with no visible error to the coordinator.

Impact: LTC patients (patient_tier: plus) may be admitted without a complete medication history, increasing reconciliation errors.

Workaround: Coordinators must manually enter prior medications and apply the LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag in the patient's chart. This flags the case for pharmacist review within 2 hours.

ETA: 2 weeks.
Assignee: Integrations Team

title: Online appointment booking conflict error SCH-CONFLICT-88
content:
Bug ID: BUG-SCH-0445
Component: Patient Scheduling Portal — Follow-Up Booking
Discovered: 2024-05-20
Severity: P1

Description: Patients who were discharged within the preceding 48 hours receive error code SCH-CONFLICT-88 when attempting to book a follow-up appointment online. The error occurs because the discharge record has not yet been propagated to the scheduling availability index, causing the system to treat the patient as still admitted and therefore ineligible for outpatient slots.

Impact: Recently discharged patients cannot self-schedule follow-ups. This increases call-center volume and may delay post-discharge care.

Workaround: Book follow-up appointments via the phone scheduling line. Coordinators should proactively schedule before discharge when possible.

ETA: 2 weeks.
Related error: SCH-CONFLICT-88

title: HealthConnect mobile app WebRTC failure on iOS 17.4+ with app version <4.2
content:
Bug ID: BUG-TC-0091
Component: HealthConnect Mobile App — WebRTC Session Layer
Discovered: 2024-05-15
Severity: P1

Description: HealthConnect mobile app versions below 4.2 use a WebRTC library (libwebrtc 94.x) that is blocked by Apple's security policy in iOS 17.4+. Patients on iOS 17.4+ with app version <4.2 receive TC-CONN-FAIL immediately on joining a telehealth session.

Impact: Any patient on iOS 17.4+ who has not updated to HealthConnect 4.2 cannot join telehealth sessions.

Fix: Updating to HealthConnect 4.2+ resolves the issue.

Workaround (if patient cannot update): Reschedule as phone appointment. Or have patient join via web browser (Chrome 110+) on a non-iOS device.

Status: Resolved in HealthConnect 4.2. Minimum version policy now enforced on app launch.
Related tickets: PT-20240528-0188

title: Multi-provider simultaneous booking crashes scheduling portal
content:
Bug ID: BUG-SCH-0212
Component: Patient Scheduling Portal — Multi-Provider Booking (Beta)
Discovered: 2024-06-01
Severity: P2

Description: When a coordinator attempts to book a same-day appointment for a patient with two providers on different floor schedules simultaneously, the scheduling portal returns a blank screen and crashes the browser tab. The booking is not saved.

Impact: Plus-tier patients who require multi-specialty same-day visits (e.g., cardiologist + physiotherapist) cannot use the multi-provider booking feature.

Workaround: Book multi-provider appointments as sequential single-provider bookings using the standard booking flow.

ETA: Under investigation. Multi-provider booking is a beta feature (SCH-ENHANCEMENT-12).
Assignee: Scheduling Platform Team

title: Patient Admission Runbook — Standard Workflow
content:
Runbook: ICD-ADM-001
Version: 3.2 | Last reviewed: 2024-03-01

Purpose: Standard workflow for admitting a patient through the Healthcare-App portal.

Step 1 — Pre-admission verification
  1a. Verify patient identity: legal name, DOB, MRN (format MRN-XXXXXX).
  1b. Confirm insurance eligibility via the Insurance Verification tab. If pre-authorization is required, initiate AUTH request and note the AUTH code.
  1c. For LTC patients (patient_tier: plus): run LTC medication sync. If sync fails, apply LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag and notify pharmacist.

Step 2 — Admission entry
  2a. Create Encounter record: type=ADM, generate ENC-ADM-XXXXX identifier.
  2b. Select ward and bed assignment. Confirm with charge nurse.
  2c. Enter primary diagnosis ICD-10 code.

Step 3 — Medication reconciliation
  3a. Pull prior medication list. If BUG-EHR-2201 is active, enter manually.
  3b. Pharmacist must countersign reconciliation within 4 hours of admission.

Step 4 — Orders
  4a. Attending physician enters admission orders.
  4b. Verify no duplicate orders (watch for BUG-EHR-2301 during peak hours).

Escalation: For P0 issues during admission, call charge nurse + pharmacy lead simultaneously.

title: Medication Administration Record (MAR) Discrepancy Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-MED-004
Version: 2.1 | Last reviewed: 2024-04-15

Purpose: Steps to take when a MAR discrepancy is identified (duplicate orders, missing doses, wrong strength).

Trigger conditions:
  - Two identical medication orders appear in MAR (likely BUG-EHR-2301)
  - A medication order is present but no administration record exists past the scheduled time
  - Nurse reports a dose was administered but MAR shows blank

Immediate steps (complete within 15 minutes):
  1. DO NOT administer either dose until pharmacy confirms the correct order.
  2. Apply MAR-DISCREPANCY flag to the patient's chart.
  3. Notify pharmacy lead by phone (not message-only).
  4. Pharmacy lead reviews the MAR and confirms which order is correct.
  5. Delete the incorrect/duplicate order in the EHR.
  6. Document the discrepancy in the clinical notes.

Safety event reporting:
  - File a safety event in RL Solutions using code MED-DISP-ERR within 1 hour.
  - Notify attending physician.

Follow-up:
  - Pharmacy completes root-cause analysis within 24 hours.
  - If BUG-EHR-2301 is confirmed as root cause, tag incident with BUG-EHR-2301 for tracking.

title: Lab Result Routing Failure Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-LAB-002
Version: 1.4 | Last reviewed: 2024-02-20

Purpose: Steps when a lab result is confirmed completed by the lab but not visible in the patient's EHR chart.

Diagnosis:
  1. Check the HL7 routing log for ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL.
  2. Confirm the lab order ID (format LAB-XXXXXX-MMDD) with the lab.
  3. Verify the patient's MRN is correctly mapped in the HL7 interface table.

Immediate steps:
  1. Escalate to hl7-support@healthcare-app.internal with: MRN, lab order ID, time of completion.
  2. HL7 support will manually re-route the message (typically within 90 minutes).
  3. Confirm result appears in chart. Notify ordering physician.

Workaround (if result is clinically urgent):
  - Request a printed copy of the result directly from the lab.
  - Scan and attach to the patient's chart as a PDF with doc_type=lab_results.

Escalation: If HL7 support does not respond within 2 hours, escalate to the on-call IT manager.

title: Patient Discharge and Follow-Up Booking Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-DIS-003
Version: 2.0 | Last reviewed: 2024-05-01

Purpose: Standard workflow for discharging a patient and ensuring follow-up care is scheduled.

Step 1 — Discharge preparation (day before)
  1a. Confirm discharge orders are signed by attending.
  1b. Pharmacist completes discharge medication reconciliation.
  1c. Schedule follow-up appointment BEFORE discharge to avoid SCH-CONFLICT-88.
      Note: If patient books online within 48 hours of discharge, they will encounter BUG-SCH-0445.
      Workaround: Book via phone scheduling line or book in-system before discharge.

Step 2 — Discharge day
  2a. Create Encounter record: type=DIS, generate ENC-DIS-XXXXX identifier.
  2b. Print discharge instructions and review with patient.
  2c. Confirm follow-up appointment details are on discharge paperwork.

Step 3 — Post-discharge
  3a. EHR discharge record propagates to scheduling index within 48 hours.
  3b. If patient calls about SCH-CONFLICT-88, direct to phone scheduling line.

Escalation: Patients with complex medication regimens should have pharmacy follow-up call within 72 hours.

title: Telehealth Connection Failure Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-TC-001
Version: 1.2 | Last reviewed: 2024-01-10

Purpose: Steps for resolving patient or provider telehealth connection failures (error TC-CONN-FAIL).

Common causes:
  - Patient device does not meet minimum requirements (camera, microphone, browser version)
  - Unstable internet connection (<5 Mbps upload)
  - Browser not granting camera/microphone permissions
  - VPN blocking WebRTC traffic
  - Outdated HealthConnect mobile app (need version 4.2+; see BUG-TC-0091)

Troubleshooting steps for patient-side failure:
  1. Guide patient through HealthConnect device-check at app.healthcare-app.com/device-check.
  2. Verify browser is Chrome 110+ or Firefox 110+.
  3. Check camera and microphone permissions in browser settings.
  4. Ask patient to disable VPN if active.
  5. If on mobile, ensure the HealthConnect mobile app is version 4.2 or above.

Troubleshooting steps for provider-side failure:
  1. Check provider workstation meets requirements.
  2. Restart the HealthConnect session from the scheduling module.

Escalation: If issue persists after 10 minutes, reschedule as phone appointment and file ticket with telehealth-support@healthcare-app.internal.

title: Insurance Pre-Authorization Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-INS-001
Version: 2.3 | Last reviewed: 2024-04-01

Purpose: Workflow for obtaining and managing insurance pre-authorization for admissions and procedures.

Step 1 — Check pre-auth requirement
  1a. Open the Insurance Verification tab for the patient.
  1b. If AUTH-REQUIRED flag is shown, pre-authorization must be obtained before admission.
  1c. If AUTH-4012 error is shown, the existing auth token has expired — re-submit with a refreshed token.

Step 2 — Submit pre-authorization
  2a. Select the procedure/admission type.
  2b. Attach supporting clinical documentation (diagnosis, physician order).
  2c. Submit to payer via the Insurance portal.
  2d. Note AUTH code returned (format AUTH-XXXX).

Step 3 — Approved
  3a. Record AUTH code in the patient's encounter record.
  3b. Proceed with admission or procedure.

Step 4 — Denied or Pending
  4a. If denied: initiate appeals process per ICD-INS-002.
  4b. If pending >2 hours for urgent cases: call payer directly.

Note: AUTH-4012 is an expired token error, not a denial. Re-submit with refreshed credentials.

title: Appointment Scheduling Conflict Resolution Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-SCH-002
Version: 1.1 | Last reviewed: 2024-05-25

Purpose: Resolving SCH-CONFLICT-88 and other appointment scheduling conflicts.

SCH-CONFLICT-88 — Post-discharge booking block:
  Cause: Patient's discharge record has not yet propagated to the scheduling index (takes up to 48 hours).
  Immediate workaround: Book via the phone scheduling line (ext. 4400).
  Permanent fix: ETA per BUG-SCH-0445 — approximately 2 weeks.

Other conflict codes:
  SCH-CONFLICT-01: Provider not available. Select an alternate provider or date.
  SCH-CONFLICT-22: Slot already booked by another patient. Refresh availability and retry.
  SCH-CONFLICT-55: Patient has a pending admission — outpatient booking blocked. Resolve admission status first.

Best practice: For discharged patients, always attempt to schedule follow-up BEFORE discharge to avoid SCH-CONFLICT-88.

Escalation: For unresolvable conflicts, contact the scheduling supervisor at scheduling-ops@healthcare-app.internal.

title: LTC Patient Coordination Runbook — Admission to Discharge
content:
Runbook: ICD-LTC-001
Version: 1.0 | Last reviewed: 2024-05-01

Purpose: Specific coordination steps for patient_tier=plus (long-term care) patients from admission to discharge.

Admission:
  1. Assign dedicated care coordinator within 30 minutes of admission.
  2. Verify LTC medication sync completed. If silent timeout occurs (BUG-EHR-2201): apply LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag, enter medications manually, notify pharmacist immediately.
  3. Cross-check medication count against referral document — do not assume sync was complete.
  4. For Plus patients arriving without a referring facility fax: contact HIM for state LTC registry lookup.

During stay:
  5. Daily medication reconciliation review (higher risk of omissions for LTC patients).
  6. Dedicated coordinator to check in with patient and family daily.

Discharge:
  7. Schedule follow-up with primary care physician AND LTC facility (if patient returning).
  8. Confirm the receiving LTC facility has received discharge summary and medication list.
  9. Pharmacist follow-up call within 72 hours (mandatory for Plus tier).

Escalation: Any Plus patient safety event must also be reported to the Plus Care Program Lead.

title: Patient Account Management Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-ACCT-001
Version: 1.3 | Last reviewed: 2024-03-15

Purpose: Steps for common patient account management tasks in the HealthConnect Admin panel.

Account unlock (locked after 5 failed login attempts):
  1. Open HealthConnect Admin panel → Patient Accounts tab.
  2. Search by MRN or name.
  3. Click 'Unlock Account'. Account is immediately accessible.
  4. Advise patient to reset their password via 'Forgot Password' before next login.

Resend activation email:
  1. Confirm email address is correct in the patient record.
  2. Click 'Resend Activation' in Admin panel.
  3. Wait 5 minutes. If not received, check spam folder.
  4. If address is wrong: correct it first, then resend.

Password reset loop on mobile (see PT-20240603-0441):
  1. Unlock account via Admin panel.
  2. Click 'Reset Portal Access' to issue a new temporary password.
  3. Email the temporary password to the patient.

MFA issues:
  - If patient lost MFA device: disable MFA via Admin panel, advise patient to set up new MFA on next login.

Escalation: For account issues not resolvable via Admin panel, contact it-helpdesk@healthcare-app.internal.

title: Post-EHR Upgrade Verification Runbook
content:
Runbook: ICD-EHR-UPG-001
Version: 1.0 | Last reviewed: 2024-06-10

Purpose: Verification steps that coordinators must perform on the morning after any EHR platform upgrade.

Background: An EHR upgrade on 2024-06-09 resulted in missing medication orders for a small time window (23:00–01:00) during the upgrade. See PT-20240610-0515.

Verification checklist (complete by 07:00 on upgrade day):
  1. For each active patient: open the MAR and compare with the prior shift's printed MAR or screenshot.
  2. Flag any medication listed in the prior shift's MAR that is missing from the current MAR.
  3. Apply MAR-DISCREPANCY flag and notify the pharmacist for each missing medication.
  4. Do not start medication passes until verification is complete for your assigned patients.
  5. If more than 5 discrepancies are found: escalate immediately to the EHR Platform Team and Patient Safety Officer — this indicates a systemic migration failure.

For lab results: verify all pending lab orders from the previous 24 hours are still showing as pending (not dropped). If results are missing, escalate per ICD-LAB-002.

Sign-off: Charge nurse must countersign the post-upgrade verification log before 08:00.

title: FAQ: What do I do if a patient's MRN is not found in the system?
content:
Question: What do I do if a patient's MRN is not found when I search the portal?

Answer: If an MRN search returns no results, follow these steps:

1. Verify the MRN format — it must be MRN-XXXXXX (6 digits). Common errors: missing hyphen, wrong number of digits.
2. Try searching by legal name and date of birth instead.
3. Check if the patient may have been registered under a different name (married vs. maiden name).
4. If the patient was referred from an external facility, their record may not yet be imported. Contact HIM (Health Information Management) at him@healthcare-app.internal to initiate an MPI (Master Patient Index) merge or new registration.
5. For urgent admissions where no MRN can be found: create a temporary encounter (type=TEMP) and notify HIM within 1 hour.

Do not create a duplicate MRN — this causes serious downstream problems including incorrect medication orders and billing errors.

title: FAQ: How do I report a suspected medication administration error?
content:
Question: How do I report a suspected medication administration error or near-miss?

Answer: Follow the steps in ICD-MED-004 immediately. In summary:

1. Apply MAR-DISCREPANCY flag to the patient's chart.
2. Notify pharmacy lead by phone within 15 minutes.
3. Do NOT administer any dose until pharmacy confirms the correct order.
4. File a safety event in RL Solutions (code MED-DISP-ERR) within 1 hour.
5. Notify the attending physician.

Remember: patient safety takes priority over workflow speed. When in doubt, hold the medication and verify.

For systemic issues (multiple patients affected): also notify the Patient Safety Officer and the EHR Platform Team. Reference BUG-EHR-2301 if the duplicate appears to be system-generated.

title: FAQ: Lab results are showing as pending but the lab says they're complete
content:
Question: The lab has confirmed a result is ready, but the EHR chart still shows it as 'pending'. What should I do?

Answer: This is most likely a HL7 routing failure (error code ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL). Follow ICD-LAB-002:

1. Get the lab order ID (format LAB-XXXXXX-MMDD) and MRN from the lab.
2. Email hl7-support@healthcare-app.internal with: patient MRN, lab order ID, time result was completed.
3. HL7 support will manually re-route — typical resolution: 90 minutes.
4. If the result is clinically urgent, request a printed copy from the lab and attach it to the chart as a PDF.

Do not wait more than 30 minutes before escalating if the result is clinically urgent (e.g., critical values, pre-procedure labs).

title: FAQ: Patient can't book a follow-up appointment after discharge
content:
Question: A recently discharged patient is calling because they can't book a follow-up online. They're getting an error. What should I do?

Answer: This is most likely BUG-SCH-0445 (error code SCH-CONFLICT-88). It affects patients who were discharged within the last 48 hours.

Immediate solution for the patient:
  Direct them to call the phone scheduling line (ext. 4400 from inside the hospital, or the patient-facing number on their discharge paperwork). Staff will book manually.

Preventive action:
  For future patients, schedule the follow-up appointment before discharge using ICD-DIS-003. This avoids the issue entirely.

Expected fix: BUG-SCH-0445 ETA is approximately 2 weeks. Until then, the phone scheduling line is the workaround.

title: FAQ: Telehealth session won't connect — TC-CONN-FAIL error
content:
Question: A patient or provider is getting error TC-CONN-FAIL when trying to join a telehealth session. How do I help them?

Answer: Follow ICD-TC-001. The most common causes are:
  - Browser permissions not granted for camera/microphone
  - Outdated browser (need Chrome 110+ or Firefox 110+)
  - VPN blocking the connection
  - Mobile app version below 4.2 (see BUG-TC-0091)

Quick guide to the patient:
  1. Go to app.healthcare-app.com/device-check — this runs a full compatibility test and shows exactly what needs to be fixed.
  2. If the check passes but the error persists, disable VPN and retry.

If the issue cannot be resolved within 10 minutes, reschedule as a phone appointment and file a support ticket at telehealth-support@healthcare-app.internal.

title: FAQ: What is AUTH-4012 and is it the same as a denial?
content:
Question: Our portal shows error AUTH-4012 on a pre-authorization submission. Does this mean the insurance company denied us?

Answer: No. AUTH-4012 is NOT a denial — it is an authentication failure. Specifically, it means the API token used to communicate with the payer has expired.

What to do:
  1. In the Insurance Verification module, click 'Refresh Credentials'.
  2. Re-submit the pre-authorization request.
  3. The payer has not seen or assessed your submission yet — there is nothing to appeal.

Why it happens: Payers rotate their API keys periodically (every 24–48 hours). If a key rotates overnight, the cached token in our system becomes stale.

Common mistake: Coordinators have escalated AUTH-4012 as a denial, causing unnecessary delays and patient distress. Always check the error code before assuming a denial. See also ICD-INS-001 and tickets PT-20240601-0411, PT-20240609-0491.

title: FAQ: How do I help a patient who is locked out of the HealthConnect portal?
content:
Question: A patient says they are locked out of the HealthConnect portal and cannot log in. How do I help them?

Answer: The most likely cause is that they exceeded the 5 failed login attempt threshold, which triggers an automatic 15-minute lockout.

If within the 15-minute window: advise patient to wait and try again.

If they need immediate access (e.g., to check pre-procedure instructions):
  1. Open the HealthConnect Admin panel.
  2. Search for the patient by MRN or name.
  3. Click 'Unlock Account'. This immediately clears the lockout.
  4. Advise patient to use 'Forgot Password' to reset before their next login attempt.

For password reset loop issues on the mobile app: see PT-20240603-0441 and ICD-ACCT-001 for the 'Reset Portal Access' workaround.

Note: Staff cannot view or retrieve a patient's existing password — only reset it. Never share or confirm passwords over the phone.

title: Healthcare-App Web Portal — Admission Module Overview
content:
Product: Healthcare-App Web Portal
Module: Admission
Version: 5.3

The Admission module enables care coordinators to register and admit patients. Key features:

1. Patient search by MRN (format MRN-XXXXXX), name, or DOB.
2. Insurance eligibility check with pre-auth initiation (see ICD-INS-001 for AUTH-4012 errors).
3. Encounter creation: type=ADM generates ENC-ADM-XXXXX.
4. Ward and bed assignment with real-time occupancy view.
5. LTC medication sync for patient_tier=plus patients (falls back to manual entry if BUG-EHR-2201 is active).
6. Admission order entry with duplicate detection (may miss duplicates during BUG-EHR-2301 window).

Known limitations:
  - LTC sync: see BUG-EHR-2201
  - Duplicate medication orders: see BUG-EHR-2301

Access: Web only. Mobile portal shows read-only admission summary.

title: HealthConnect Mobile App — Patient-Facing Features
content:
Product: HealthConnect Mobile App (iOS/Android)
Version: 4.2+

Patient-facing features:
  - View upcoming and past appointments
  - Book follow-up appointments (note: BUG-SCH-0445 may affect recently discharged patients)
  - Access test results (note: lab results may be delayed if ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL is active)
  - Telehealth session join (requires version 4.2+; see ICD-TC-001 for TC-CONN-FAIL)

Minimum requirements:

  - Stable internet connection (5 Mbps+ for video)

For staff: The HealthConnect Admin panel (web only) manages patient access, resets PINs, and handles account lockouts.

title: Lab Results Integration — HL7 v2.x Interface Specification
content:
Product: Healthcare-App HL7 Integration Layer
Interface: Lab Results (ORU^R01)
Version: 2.4.1

Overview: Lab results are transmitted from the laboratory information system (LIS) to the EHR via HL7 v2.x ORU^R01 messages. The HL7 listener processes these messages and updates the patient chart.

Message flow:
  LIS → HL7 Listener → EHR Chart (lab_results section)

Known issue: ERR_HL7_ROUTE_FAIL — occurs intermittently when MSH-11 is set to 'D' (debug). See ICD-LAB-002 for workaround.

Lab order ID format: LAB-XXXXXX-MMDD
  - XXXXXX: 6-digit MRN
  - MMDD: month-day of order
  Example: LAB-293847-0512 = CBC ordered on May 12 for MRN-293847

Critical value handling: The HL7 listener sends an automated page to the ordering provider when a result is flagged as critical (OBX-8 = 'HH' or 'LL'). If the result does not appear in the chart, this page may also fail. Always verify chart delivery for critical results.

title: HealthConnect Telehealth Platform — Technical Overview
content:
Product: HealthConnect Telehealth Platform
Version: 3.1

Technology stack: WebRTC-based video sessions. Signaling via WebSocket. Session management integrated with the scheduling module.

Error TC-CONN-FAIL:
  Triggered when WebRTC cannot establish a peer-to-peer connection. Most common causes: firewall/VPN blocking WebRTC ports (UDP 3478, 5349), browser permissions denied, outdated browser or mobile app (BUG-TC-0091).

Device requirements:
  - Chrome 110+ or Firefox 110+
  - Camera + microphone access granted
  - No VPN (or VPN with WebRTC passthrough enabled)
  - Minimum 5 Mbps upload/download
  - HealthConnect mobile app 4.2+ for iOS/Android sessions

Device check tool: app.healthcare-app.com/device-check
  Runs automated tests for browser version, media permissions, network bandwidth, and WebRTC connectivity.

Session recording: Recordings are stored in the secure media vault (HIPAA-compliant). Retention: 7 years.

Related: ICD-TC-001, FAQ-TC-001

title: Insurance Verification Module — Product Documentation
content:
Product: Healthcare-App Insurance Verification Module
Version: 4.0

Features:
  - Real-time eligibility check via payer API integration
  - Pre-authorization submission and tracking
  - AUTH code management (format AUTH-XXXX)
  - Denial and appeals workflow (ICD-INS-002)

Common error codes:
  AUTH-4012: Auth token expired. Re-submit with refreshed credentials. The token expires after 24 hours of inactivity or if the payer rotates keys. Resolution: see ICD-INS-001 Step 1c and FAQ-INS-001.

Pre-auth required indicators:
  - AUTH-REQUIRED flag shown when selected procedure requires pre-authorization
  - Mandatory for: elective surgeries, MRI/CT scans, specialist referrals for some payers

Payer integration status:
  - 47 of 52 major payers: real-time eligibility
  - 5 payers: batch processing (results within 2 hours)

Note: The Insurance Verification Module is web-only. Mobile shows eligibility status (read-only).

title: Patient Scheduling Portal — Product Documentation
content:
Product: Patient Scheduling Portal (web and mobile)
Version: 6.1

Key features:
  - Provider search by specialty, location, language
  - Real-time slot availability
  - Follow-up appointment booking (note: BUG-SCH-0445 affects post-discharge patients)
  - Appointment reminders via SMS and email
  - Cancellation and rescheduling
  - Telehealth appointment booking and joining

Scheduling conflict codes:
  SCH-CONFLICT-88: Discharge record not yet propagated (BUG-SCH-0445). Workaround: phone line.
  SCH-CONFLICT-01: Provider unavailable.
  SCH-CONFLICT-22: Slot double-booked.
  SCH-CONFLICT-55: Patient still has active admission — cannot book outpatient.

Integration with EHR: The scheduling index syncs with the EHR admission/discharge status every 48 hours (current limitation — being reduced to real-time in next release).

Related runbooks: ICD-SCH-002, ICD-DIS-003

title: Patient Account and Portal Access Management
content:
Product: Patient Account Management
Version: 2.5

Account types:
  - Regular: standard access to appointments, results, messaging
  - Plus (patient_tier=plus): additional LTC coordination features, priority scheduling, dedicated care coordinator

Common account issues:
  - Locked account: 5 failed login attempts locks the account for 15 minutes. Coordinator can unlock via HealthConnect Admin panel.
  - Password reset: patient initiates via portal or calls support. Staff cannot view passwords.
  - Portal access: newly registered patients receive activation email within 1 hour.
  - MFA: patients can use SMS, email, or authenticator app.

For staff account issues: contact it-helpdesk@healthcare-app.internal.
For patient account issues: use the HealthConnect Admin panel (web portal, Admin tab).

Related: PROD-MOB-001, ICD-ACCT-001

title: Discharge Module — Product Documentation
content:
Product: Healthcare-App Web Portal
Module: Discharge
Version: 5.3

The Discharge module manages the full patient discharge workflow. Key features:

1. Discharge order sign-off: attending physician signature required (digital or in-person).
2. Medication reconciliation: generates discharge medication list from inpatient MAR. Pharmacist countersign required for anticoagulants and high-alert medications.
3. Encounter close-out: type=DIS, generates ENC-DIS-XXXXX identifier.
4. Discharge instructions: printable PDF and email delivery.
5. Follow-up scheduling: book outpatient follow-up from within the discharge workflow (recommended to avoid BUG-SCH-0445).
6. LTC return coordination: for Plus patients, triggers notification to receiving LTC facility.

Known limitations:
  - Post-discharge follow-up booking within 48 hours triggers SCH-CONFLICT-88 (BUG-SCH-0445).
  - Print queue failures: generate and email PDF as fallback (see PT-20240610-0509).
  - Discharge record propagation to scheduling index: up to 48 hours.

Related: ICD-DIS-003, FAQ-DIS-001

title: Plus (LTC) Patient Tier — Feature Overview
content:
Product: Healthcare-App Plus Tier (patient_tier=plus)
Version: 2.0

The Plus tier is designed for long-term care (LTC) patients who require enhanced coordination between the hospital and their home facility.

Plus-tier features:
  - Automatic assignment of a dedicated care coordinator within 30 minutes of admission.
  - LTC medication sync: attempts to pull prior medication list from the state LTC registry on admission.
    Status: BUG-EHR-2201 is currently active — sync may silently fail. Workaround: LTC-MANUAL-SYNC flag + manual entry.
  - Priority scheduling: Plus patients can book same-day appointments without availability constraints.
  - Pharmacist follow-up call within 72 hours of discharge (mandatory).
  - Extended discharge summary delivered to the receiving LTC facility.
  - Family communication hub: secure messaging accessible by family members with patient consent.

Known issue: BUG-EHR-2201 — LTC medication sync failure. Active. ETA: 2 weeks. See ICD-LTC-001 for workaround.

Related runbooks: ICD-ADM-001, ICD-LTC-001, ICD-DIS-003

title: EHR Platform Overview — Ordering Module and MAR
content:
Product: Healthcare-App EHR Platform
Module: Ordering and Medication Administration Record (MAR)
Version: 8.1.2

The Ordering module allows physicians and pharmacists to enter, review, and manage medication and procedure orders. The MAR displays all current medication orders with administration schedule and history.

Key features:
  - Real-time order entry with drug-allergy checking.
  - Duplicate order detection (note: BUG-EHR-2301 may cause missed duplicates during high-concurrency periods).
  - MAR-DISCREPANCY flag: applied by coordinators when a discrepancy is suspected. Triggers pharmacist review within 30 minutes.
  - Order history: full audit trail retained for 7 years.
  - Upgrade management: post-upgrade verification required per ICD-EHR-UPG-001.

Known issues:
  - BUG-EHR-2301: concurrent de-duplication failure. Active. ETA: next maintenance window.
  - Post-upgrade order migration gaps: see PT-20240610-0515 and ICD-EHR-UPG-001.

Allergy checking: Drug names must be entered from the standardized dropdown. Free-form entries may bypass allergy matching.

Related runbooks: ICD-MED-004, ICD-EHR-UPG-001
